events.label: TSMC Q2 results known (record beat: $40.2B / EPS $4.31 / GM 67.7% / capex $60-64B / wafer hike 5-10% all nodes); management call 2pm ET; Netflix Q2 AH (~4pm ET); PayPal $53B Stripe/Advent bid
events.note: TSMC Q2 results confirmed ~2 AM ET: revenue $40.2B (record, +36% YoY), EPS $4.31 vs $3.87 consensus (+11%), gross margin 67.7%, net income +77.4% YoY — 5th consecutive record quarterly profit. FY 2026 guidance raised to >40% USD (from >30%). 2026 CapEx raised to $60-64B (from $52-56B). CRITICAL: TSMC confirmed wafer price hike 5-10% across ALL advanced nodes (3nm, 5nm, AND 7nm = 74% of wafer revenue) — broader than prior 3nm-only reports. Clients: NVDA, AMD, AAPL, QCOM, AVGO. NVDA premarket -7.2% ($197). Korea Kospi -7.3%. Management call 2pm ET is the day's decisive event. Netflix Q2 after close: est. EPS $0.79, revenue $12.57B. Stripe/Advent bid $60.50/share (~$53B) for PayPal announced; PYPL +18%; Polymarket 82% deal-close probability.

events.label: PayPal (PYPL) — Stripe / Advent International $60.50/share acquisition bid (~$53B)
events.note: Stripe and Advent International jointly bid $60.50/share (~$53B total enterprise value) to acquire PayPal, backed by ~$50B in committed debt financing. Combined entity would process an estimated $3.7 trillion in annual payment volume. PYPL +18% on July 16. Board meeting to formally respond expected July 20. Deal spread implies DOJ antitrust risk on Stripe-PayPal combination; Polymarket 82% deal-close probability. Largest proposed fintech M&A deal in years.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 earnings (after close) + IBM full Q2 earnings call + GOOGL Q2 earnings (after close) — triple clearing event
events.note: TSLA: Q2 earnings follow the blowout July 2 delivery report (480K vs 406K consensus). Need gross margin recovery (>25%), FSD revenue recognition at scale, Q3 delivery guide >450K for re-rate above $420. IBM: full Q2 call gives context on the software-to-hardware budget rotation that caused IBM's -25% worst day on record July 14. CEO must clarify: one-quarter or multi-year? GOOGL Q2: AI Overviews monetization, Search share vs AI competitors, and capex trajectory are the market-moving variables. AMD AI Day runs July 22-23 concurrently (MI400 roadmap).

events.label: AMD AI Day — San Francisco (Jul 22-23) — MI400 roadmap, competitive positioning vs NVDA
events.note: AMD's annual AI event in San Francisco runs July 22-23. First major deep-dive on the MI400 series roadmap since Computex. UBS raised AMD PT to $700, Rosenblatt to $665. The TSMC wafer price hike (5-10% across all advanced nodes) complicates AMD's margin picture but TSMC's capex raise to $60-64B expands fab capacity available to AMD. Event could be a re-rating catalyst if AMD provides hyperscaler win disclosures alongside competitive NVDA commentary. Context: NVDA's wafer hike exposure (GB200/H100 on 4nm/5nm nodes) may create an opening for AMD's MI400 cost positioning.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — July hike probability now ~20%; no-hike expected; September language is the signal
events.note: June CPI undershoot (-0.4% MoM / 3.5% YoY) collapsed July hike probability from 40%+ to ~20% on July 14. No July hike now the strong base case. The FOMC statement language on September and the 2026 dot-plot update will be the market signal. If dots shift September hike lower: BUY upgrade likely. If dots maintain September hike risk: 30Y re-accelerates. Warsh's two Congressional testimonies (July 14-15) set the backdrop for no escalation.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business first quantification; peak Q2 earnings week (GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN also)
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). GOOGL, MSFT, and AMZN also report in late July — peak Q2 earnings risk window. IBM's enterprise software warning (July 14) adds a risk factor: MSFT Azure consulting and enterprise software could face read-across pressure. META's ad-driven model is insulated from IBM's enterprise IT budget rotation.

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — captures WTI +9.4% spike (Jul 13) + Iran Hormuz blockade oil pass-through
events.note: June CPI (July 14) captured pre-Hormuz-shock prices and printed -0.4% MoM / 3.5% YoY. July CPI will be the FIRST month to reflect the WTI +9.4% spike of July 13 and the ongoing Strait disruption. If the Hormuz blockade persists through late July, July CPI could surprise significantly to the upside relative to June — erasing the July 14 disinflation narrative. This is the real inflation inflection event for H2 2026. The 30Y's failure to rally meaningfully on July 14 (only -0.4bps) suggests the bond market is already pricing this risk.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle fundamental clearing event
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. TSMC Q2 (July 16) confirmed the AI demand thesis with $40.2B revenue and FY guidance raised to >40% USD — but TSMC's 5-10% wafer price hike across ALL advanced nodes (including 5nm, NVDA's primary manufacturing node) introduces a 2-4pp gross margin headwind for NVDA that management must address. NVDA -7.2% premarket July 16 on the wafer hike announcement. Full-size add gate for NVDA: sustained close above $200 + wafer hike impact clarified in NVDA guidance + VIX <16.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX Nasdaq-100 effective July 7; inclusion-day distribution confirmed at $158.77 peak. Re-entry gate: two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume. First earnings (Starlink subscriber/ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event after the inclusion-day distribution pattern. Lock-up expiry December 9 adds supply overhang.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
